tasks.title: Separate recoverable persistence admission from fatal store failure
tasks.objective: Keep expected capacity or metadata admission rejection local to one unpublished Run while preserving the fatal latch for failures that make durable state untrustworthy.
tasks.outcome: A rejected durable start creates no child publication or partial row and does not prevent existing Runs from appending or finalizing or a later admissible Run from starting.
acceptance: Persistence errors distinguish recoverable admission rejection from database, I/O, commit, integrity, actor, and invariant failures that make the store untrustworthy.

The actor latches only fatal store failures; a running-record or metadata-capacity rejection returns the existing public persistence error for that start without freezing unrelated append, finalize, or later start commands.

An owner-local small-capacity seam proves one rejected start leaves no durable row, then a terminal record or newly available capacity permits a later start and terminal commit through the same actor.
A deterministic fatal store failure still freezes the durable cursor and rejects later mutations while already-owned live Run control remains available as ADR 009 declares.
The correction adds no schema migration, recovery class, retry loop, public fault API, or generic storage framework.

verification.proves: Persistence admission, fatal-latch, native lifecycle, and full repository regressions pass.
Recoverable admission and fatal durable-state failure semantics remain explicit at the persistence owner boundary.

tasks.title: Validate recovered native Run specifications through one semantic owner
tasks.objective: Make live launch and startup recovery share one daemon-owned RunSpec semantic validator so parseable but invalid durable rows fail before socket publication.
tasks.outcome: Every recovered native Run has a non-null launch specification satisfying the same program, terminal-size, and declared-reference invariants as a newly started Run.
acceptance: RunSpec semantic admission has one daemon-owned Rust validator reused by start, fork materialization, persistent insert, and recovered-state validation; TypeScript continues to validate the public wire shape without becoming daemon admission truth.
The native persistence format rejects null RunSpec, empty program, zero rows or columns, and empty declared-input references as corrupt state before the daemon publishes its socket.
Persistent insert fails closed if a caller attempts to store non-native backend identity, non-native capabilities, a missing spec, or an invalid spec; no partial row or Run publication occurs.
Real restart corruption fixtures prove no Rust, TypeScript, CLI, or attachment client can observe a rejected Run or a partially exposed valid sibling.
The correction adds no tmux persistence, PID adoption, schema migration, salvage path, or Backend abstraction.

verification.proves: Shared RunSpec validation, real restart corruption, cross-client validation, and full repository regressions pass.
The recovered native Run domain and pre-publication corruption boundary are documented.

documentation.rationale: Persistence admission hardening; the same decision record owns its contract.

learning.rationale: Archived before the closeout review contract existed; no review was recorded at the time and none is reconstructed now.

promotion.rationale: No learning was captured for this historical Feature, so there is nothing to route or promote.
